Great questions — thanks for sharing the sample. Recap + proposed next steps below. I copied Rishi for architecture and Dev for SDK specifics.

High-level recommendations (PoC scope):
1) SDK quickstart (1–2 days): use Redwood JS or Python SDK; there is a one-file example that wires auth, example schema validation, and streaming. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts
2) Auth: for initial PoC use short-lived API keys (rotated via our Console + KMS). For production in your Private deployment we recommend mTLS for strict network-level controls and optional OAuth2 service tokens for user-scoped calls. We can provide a mTLS bootstrap script.
3) Routing policy: configure region-first with fallback to a compatible model variant. Policy example: primary:us-west2 -> fallback:cds-quantized-1. Routing and fallback are configurable per-route in the Console.
4) Structured output reliability: multi-layer strategy below:
   - Constrained decoding: at the model level we apply constrained tokenization and deterministic sampling for key output fields (structured output mode).
   - Schema enforcement: enforce JSON Schema v4 on the client (SDK) using our recommended validators before accepting output.
   - Server-side post-parse validation: Redwood can run a post-processing validation hook that returns structured error codes when schema mismatches occur.
   - Retry pattern: for transient schema failures, do 2 fast retries (100ms -> 400ms) with the same prompt + soft-constraints; if still invalid, escalate to deterministic reformat endpoint (no sampling) or return a specific error to your app so it can fall back to last-known-good or ask user for clarification.

Next steps / owners:
- Dev (dev@redwood.com): draft PoC skeleton and attach sample schema (ETA: 48 hours).
- Rishi: schedule architecture deep-dive (45 min) to discuss mTLS, KMS, and routing policies (ETA: propose times).
- Ella / Finlytics: confirm availability and any compliance constraints (data retention, audit logs).

On 2027-03-22 Soojin Lee wrote:
> - Constrained decoding: at the model level we apply constrained tokenization and deterministic sampling for key output fields (structured output mode).
> - Schema enforcement: enforce JSON Schema v4 on the client (SDK) using our recommended validators before accepting output.

Quick technical notes from the SDK side:
- SDKs: official packages for node (>=16) and python (>=3.9). Quickstart creates a ValidationMiddleware that runs after the generation response:
  - JS example: use ajv for schema validation (we include schema loader + version check). If ajv.errors, the middleware returns an error object: { code: "STRUCT_SCHEMA_MISMATCH", details: [...] }
  - Python example: jsonschema.validate with the same schema bundle.
- Schema versioning: include a schema_version in the prompt context and require the service to return schema_version in response metadata; clients reject mismatched versions.
- Retry semantics: implement idempotent request IDs (X-Request-ID) and exponential backoff for validation failures. Two automatic retries are safe if the prompt is unchanged. For deterministic reformatting we call the /structured/reformat endpoint (no sampling) which is billed differently but returns canonical JSON.
- Error codes to expect from Redwood: STRUCT_SCHEMA_MISMATCH, STRUCT_REFORMAT_TRIGGERED, MODEL_FALLBACK_USED. Use these to surface precise UX messages.

I'll draft a PoC repo and attach the sample_schema_v1.json into the Drive folder. ETA: EOD tomorrow.

— Dev
SDK Engineer, Redwood Inference
